OUTCOME

Accepted: the selected model passed the selection gate and all three test gates.

Model Card

No Databallr counterpart: Databallr reads ShotQuality's paid tracking model, which publishes no model card. This one is built from the registration.

WHAT IT PREDICTS

Each field-goal attempt is made (1) or missed (0). Expected points = shot value (2 or 3) x make probability. Field-goal points only: free throws are not modelled, because a fouled missed shot is not a field-goal attempt and is absent from the shot data.

WHAT IT READS

Before the shot only: location (x, y, distance, zone), shot value, the NBA's shot-type label (driving, pull-up, step-back, floating, dunk, putback and so on), period, seconds left in the period, score margin, seconds since the team gained possession (a transition proxy) and whether the possession had an offensive rebound. Never the shooter's identity and never whether the shot was assisted (the play-by-play records assists only on makes).

CANDIDATES

Fixed before any fit: Logistic regression, distance splines; LightGBM, 31 leaves; LightGBM, 127 leave

textSample:
RESEARCH METRIC
Registered 2026-11-05
zTS: Scoring Efficiency and Playtype Difficulty

Relative true shooting adjusted for the difficulty of a player's play-type mix, and what that buys.

Scoring efficiency has been refined one step at a time. FG% counted makes. eFG% gave threes their extra point. TS% folded in free throws, so every scoring attempt counts. rTS measured that against the league, because scoring environments change from season to season.

Each step kept the same question and answered it more completely. None of them asks what kind of possession produced the attempt.

A cut and an isolation count the same in every one of those numbers. They are not equally hard.

Two Signals in One Number

A player's efficiency mixes two things: how well he scored, and the kind of possessions he was asked to score on. Move a player into easier finishing chances and his TS% rises without him becoming a better scorer. Hand him more creation and it can fall while his scoring barely changes.

Box-score efficiency keeps the results of those possessions and drops the role that produced them.

The gap between roles is large. In 2025-26, isolation possessions converted at 52.0 play-type TS and cuts at 69.6, against a league average of 58.2.

zTS makes the role explicit. It looks at a player's play-type mix and asks what a league-average scorer would shoot on exactly that mix. A low expectation means a hard role; a high one, an easy role. The gap between the league average and that expect
